The lesson says what to pick but not where the connector is on the n8n canvas, so a first-time builder cannot tell how to attach them.
A box on a canvas is not a loop. Readers may look for a loop node and not find one.
Here a workflow reads as the opposite of an agent, but Step 3 calls a workflow an agentic system. The reader cannot tell whether a workflow counts as an agent.
Step 2 already defined an agent as an LLM with tools in a loop. Step 3 adds agentic system as an umbrella, so two layers of names arrive in one step.
choice.name and choice.args appear with no explanation of what ask_model returns, so the reader cannot follow the loop's data.
The Before you start card on the same page says about 25 minutes, and setting up Python, a notebook, a virtual environment and an OpenAI account takes longer than 10.

override=True is never explained in the prose. Readers who wonder what it does have to guess.
Step 4 already calls sending to many models parallelization. This caveat only appears after the Step 5 code, so the reader meets the word before its limit.
The seven steps are shown only as a trace. The competitor loop that stores names and answers is never listed, so the reader cannot see how the lists are filled.

client is used here but never created in this lesson. The reader has to remember the notebook from Lesson 3 or guess.

The lesson never shows what history looks like (a list of message dictionaries), so the reader cannot tell what to pass in.
The lesson calls this the full JSON, but it is a Python dict with a capital F. Lesson 5 defined JSON as plain text, so the reader is unsure what they are looking at.

The steps and error hints expect linkedin.pdf, but the shipped starter and final folders contain twin/linkedin.txt. The reader cannot tell which file to use.
